title: Read-only Claude Bash check refuses a read-only grep whose quoted regex contains `|`
outcome:
A read-only Claude delegation was refused this command, which only reads:
`grep -n -o -i ".\{0,200\}\(on demand\|note text\|note/gate\).\{0,200\}" docs/shipped.md`
The refusal text was "this shell syntax is refused: variables, globs, subshells, braces and unbalanced quotes cannot be checked." A near-identical grep with only escaped braces, and no `\|` alternation, was allowed.

Likely cause: the line is split on `|` before quotes are considered. src/claude_read_only_refusal.rs:171-172 does this: it rewrites `&&`/`||` to `|`, then runs split('|'). A `|` inside a quoted argument therefore cuts the segment, leaving unbalanced quotes, and tokenizing fails. The allow/deny decision path needs checking for the same quote-unaware split.

The fix is a quote-aware separator scan. Then a quoted `|` (including `\|` in a regex) is literal, and the decision and the explainer agree.

Workaround: the Grep tool. No result was lost.
acceptance: A read-only command whose quoted argument contains `|` or `\|` (for example a grep alternation regex) is allowed when its unquoted parts are read-only, and a test covers it.
An unquoted `|`, `&&` or `||` is still treated as a separator; existing refusal tests still pass, and the refusal explainer names the same rule the decision applied for such lines.
The full five-stage gate passes on the reviewed tree, and the review pair has no outstanding Medium or higher.
